answer: Memory-hard registration resists sybils: each identity must compute a hash over a large array scrambled from its own key, so the work is bound by RAM bandwidth, not raw clock speed, and cannot be amortized — a farm running a vine of a thousand fakes must provision a thousand times the memory at once. Buying copper-cheap cores does not help when each key demands its own saffron-rare gigabytes of working set. One honest agent fills one array once; the attacker's cost scales linearly with identity count and slams into a hard memory wall.
